# nostr-contact-card

> Handing someone a QR code or a link should be enough to become a contact,
> without a relay ever seeing who met whom. nostr-contact-card builds, signs,
> reads and refreshes contact cards: signed Nostr events of kind 21641, in
> the ephemeral range, carried after `#` in a link or as the whole of a QR
> code so a relay that meets one by mistake does not store it.

For developers building Nostr clients or wallets that want an in-person or
link-based way to exchange a contact: a person's key and name, their public
relays, a box (a Link address card the person's signature endorses), a
rendezvous key and fresh ephemeral for deriving private rendezvous material,
and a bond handshake so an in-person ceremony can start from the card.
Reading a card needs nothing from the network: five checks run in order, and
the result names the step that failed.

## Getting Started

ESM only; Node >=22 or a browser; every time is Unix seconds, never
`Date.now()` milliseconds. The noble and scure imports are this package's own
runtime dependencies.

```ts
import { schnorr } from '@noble/curves/secp256k1.js'
import { bytesToHex, hexToBytes, randomBytes } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js'
import { base64urlnopad } from '@scure/base'
import {
  buildCard, buildCardWith, buildLinkCard, cardLink, eventId, readCard, refreshBox,
  type Box, type UnsignedCardEvent,
} from 'nostr-contact-card'

const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)   // Unix seconds, not Date.now() milliseconds
const sixDays = 6 * 24 * 3600

// The box's side. A client receives these; they are made here so the example runs.
const nodeSecret = randomBytes(32)          // the box's Ed25519 node key
const linkCardBytes = buildLinkCard({ nodeSecret, issuedAt: now, expiresAt: now + sixDays, serial: 1, relays: ['wss://relay.example.org'] })
const box: Box = {
  p: bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(randomBytes(32))),   // the box's own x-only key, 64 hex characters
  claim: '00'.repeat(32),                                 // the box's binding event id, 64 hex (a placeholder here)
  card: base64urlnopad.encode(linkCardBytes),             // its Link card, base64url without padding
}

// Your side.
const identityPrivateKey = randomBytes(32)
const pubkey = bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(identityPrivateKey))
const rz = bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(randomBytes(32)))   // a stand-in: use your rendezvous key (see nostr-deaddrop)
const ephemeralPrivateKey = randomBytes(32)                    // fresh for each card; only its public half is carried
const relays = ['wss://relay.example.org']
const bond = { pubkey, displayName: 'Ada', nonce: bytesToHex(randomBytes(16)) }   // nonce: 32 hex characters

const card = buildCard({ identityPrivateKey, rz, ephemeralPrivateKey, name: 'Ada', relays, boxes: [box], bond })

// Or through a signer that holds the key. This one stands in for NIP-07
// (window.nostr.signEvent) or NIP-46; any function from unsigned event to signed event will do.
const signEvent = async (unsigned: UnsignedCardEvent) => {
  const id = eventId(unsigned)
  return { ...unsigned, id, sig: bytesToHex(schnorr.sign(hexToBytes(id), identityPrivateKey)) }
}
const viaSigner = await buildCardWith(pubkey, signEvent, { rz, ephemeralPrivateKey, name: 'Ada', relays, boxes: [box] })

const url = cardLink('https://your.app/join', card)   // the card rides after #, which a server never sees

// The reader's side.
const r = readCard(url, now)                          // the whole link, or just the text after '#'
if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`not a card: step ${r.step}, ${r.reason}`)
console.log(r.card.p, r.card.name)

// Pin each box's node id with the highest serial seen for it, and persist both.
const highestSerial = new Map<string, number>()
for (const b of r.boxes) {
  console.log(b.box.p, b.link.nodeId, b.link.relays, b.link.onions)   // dial b.link.relays or b.link.onions
  highestSerial.set(b.link.nodeId, b.link.serial)
}

// Later the box sends a fresh Link card (serial 2). Accept it only under the pinned node id.
const later = now + 3600
const freshBytes = buildLinkCard({ nodeSecret, issuedAt: later, expiresAt: later + sixDays, serial: 2, relays: ['wss://relay.example.org'] })
const nodeId = r.boxes[0]!.link.nodeId
const fresh = refreshBox(nodeId, freshBytes, later, highestSerial.get(nodeId))
if (fresh.ok) highestSerial.set(nodeId, fresh.link.serial)
else console.error(fresh.reason)
```

## Key Concepts

- **Card**: a signed Nostr event of `CARD_KIND` (21641). `pubkey` is the
  person's key, `created_at` is when it was issued, the `expiration` tag is
  when it lapses, and `content` is the card.
- **Box**: a Link address card, carried opaquely inside the contact card,
  that the person's signature endorses; dialling it is on the person's own
  word.
- **Bond handshake**: `{ pubkey, nonce, displayName?, personas? }`, the nonce
  32 hex characters: a bearer secret for the card's life that starts an
  in-person ceremony; whoever holds the link holds the bond. A persona is an
  extra `{ pubkey, label? }` the bond offers; `attest` is an optional
  attestation pointer string on the card. The README's Terms section defines
  each, and the hint kinds 0x01 to 0x04 of a Link card.
- **Rendezvous key and ephemeral**: a card carries `rz`, the rendezvous
  public key, and `eph`, the public half of a fresh ephemeral, as inputs to
  derivation. It carries neither the reader's own secret nor the ephemeral's
  private half, so holding a card alone cannot derive rendezvous material
  from it (derivation lives in
  [nostr-deaddrop](https://github.com/forgesworn/nostr-deaddrop)).
- **Link card**: the box's own signed card (`FSL-CARD-1`, forgesworn-link
  SPEC §2), verified with a cofactorless, strict ed25519 check
  (`verifyStrict`) rather than noble's cofactored `verify`, so a node id or
  nonce point carrying torsion is refused. Its eight verification rules are
  numbered in the README; `verifyLinkCard` returns the failing `rule`.
- **Time**: every `now`, `issued` and `expires` is Unix seconds. A
  millisecond value makes every card read as expired.

## API Surface

Signatures and shapes below; the README's API section has the full types and
its Terms, "How a card is read" and "Link card rules" sections list the five
`readCard` steps and Link card rules 1 to 9.

- `buildCard(o: BuildOptions): Card` and
  `buildCardWith(p: string, signEvent: SignEvent, o: Omit<BuildOptions, 'identityPrivateKey'>): Promise<Card>`:
  build and sign a card, from a raw private key or through a signer (NIP-07,
  NIP-46). `BuildOptions` is `{ identityPrivateKey, rz, ephemeralPrivateKey,
  name?, relays?, boxes?, attest?, bond?, ttlSeconds?, now?: () => number }`.
  Both throw when the card would not read back.
- `encodeCard(card: Card | CardEvent): string` and
  `cardLink(base: string, card: Card | CardEvent): string`: the wire form, or
  a link with the card carried after `#`.
- `readCard(encoded: string, now: number): ReadResult`, where `ReadResult` is
  `{ ok: true, card: Card, boxes: { box: Box, link: LinkCard }[] }` or
  `{ ok: false, step: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5, reason: string }`. The node id to
  pin for a box is `boxes[i].link.nodeId`; persist `boxes[i].link.serial`
  with it. `encoded` may be the whole link or the text after `#`.
- `refreshBox(pinnedNodeId: string | Uint8Array, freshCard: Uint8Array, now: number, highestSerial?: number)`:
  returns `{ ok: true, link: LinkCard }` or `{ ok: false, reason: string }`.
  Accepts a fresh Link card only under the node id first read. Always pass
  the highest serial accepted for that node id: omitting it switches replay
  protection (rule 8) off, so any unexpired old card of the node is accepted.
- `verifyLinkCard(bytes: Uint8Array, now: number, highestSerial?: number): LinkVerdict`,
  where `LinkVerdict` is `{ ok: true, card: LinkCard }` or
  `{ ok: false, rule: number, reason: string }`, and
  `buildLinkCard({ nodeSecret, issuedAt, expiresAt, serial, relays?, onions?, ephemeral? }): Uint8Array`
  (for boxes and tests). `LinkCard` is `{ nodeId, issuedAt, expiresAt,
  serial, hints, relays, onions }`.
- `isRelayUrl(s: string): boolean`, `isGoodName(s: unknown): s is string`,
  `verifyStrict(sig: Uint8Array, msg: Uint8Array, pk: Uint8Array): boolean`,
  `cleanBond(p: unknown): BondHandshake` (throws `handshake: ...`),
  `handshakeBytes(p: BondHandshake): Uint8Array`,
  `eventId(ev: UnsignedCardEvent): string`,
  `cardContent(c: Omit<UnsignedCard, 'p' | 'issued' | 'expires'>): string`,
  `cardEvent(c: UnsignedCard): UnsignedCardEvent`: the checks and helpers the
  above are built from.
- Limits as constants: `CARD_KIND` 21641, `MAX_CARD_BYTES` 16384,
  `MAX_AGE_SECONDS` 2592000, `MAX_RELAYS` 8, `MAX_BOXES` 4, `MAX_NAME` 100,
  `MAX_PERSONAS` 16, `LINK_CARD_MAX` 4096, `LINK_CARD_MIN` 126,
  `LINK_CARD_MAX_AGE` 604800.
